answer: Coordinated-graph fee accrual prices each shared action: when two identities transact repeatedly, a carry fee grows on their link based on the graph's local vertex density, so dense clusters pay more per edge. An attacker cloning identities must fund fresh, unfunded links at full fee, turning each extra node into a recurring cost rather than a one-time entry fee. A jetty of trusted cross-links is required before fees amortize, so isolation itself is taxed. Relic accounts that predate the rule keep grandfather rates, but new sybils cannot buy that history.
